html:
SMTO-FIL-0056 — Another program is using the file SMTO needs

GUID: 5922fa72-f0f1-46ee-b24f-c2c68948d9c1
Slug: file-sharing-violation
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • Windows says another program has this file open or locked, so SMTO couldn't use it right now.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, close the file in any program that may have it open, such as Word, Excel, a text editor or a preview window. Windows blocks other programs from using a file while one program holds it.
  2. If the file is in a synced or shared folder, wait until syncing or virus scanning has finished. Sync and antivirus programs can hold a file for a short time.
  3. Ask SMTO to read the file again before changing it, then try the change once more. The other program may have changed the file, so SMTO should work from its latest version.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes with the file and reports no error for it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking SMTO to retry over and over; find and close the program holding the file first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Windows reported ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION or ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION because another process holds an open handle or lock on the file.

What this means

  • Windows reported a sharing or lock violation, preserving its more specific native code instead of a generic permission error. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Windows reported a sharing or lock violation, preserving its more specific native code instead of a generic permission error.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the actual owning handle and supported release path; this code alone does not name the process.

How to fix it

  • Identify the holding process on the Gateway host (Resource Monitor's Associated Handles search, or Sysinternals handle.exe) and close it or release its handle. Re-read the file's current revision before repeating the operation, and avoid tight retry loops.
  • Identify the owning process and close or release its handle through supported controls. Retry only after the lock is released and the file revision is refreshed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The conflict is released through supported controls and a fresh revision is checked before further mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
